t.1.4.1: Ugraśravas, the son of Lomaharṣaṇa, a sūta and teller of Purāṇic lore, approached the seers who had assembled in the Naimiṣa forest at the twelve-year sacrificial session of Śaunaka, the master of the household.
t.1.4.2: The bard, who had labored long in the lore of the Purāṇa, joined his palms in reverence and said to them: "What do you wish to hear? What shall I tell you?"
t.1.4.4: He who knows the divine tales, the stories of the gods and the asuras, and who knows in full the tales of men, serpents, and gandharvas.
t.1.4.3: The seers said to him: O Lomaharṣaṇa, we shall ask you, and you will tell us who are eager to listen, the supreme sequence of tales. But for now the blessed Śaunaka is sitting in the fire-sanctuary.
t.1.4.5: And he too, O Sauti, is present at this sacrifice: the learned twice-born head of the family, skilled, firm in his vows, wise, a teacher in the śāstra and in the Āraṇyaka.
t.1.4.6: He speaks the truth, is devoted to tranquility, is an ascetic, and is steadfast in his vows; he is worthy of honor from all of us. Let him therefore be awaited for the present.
t.1.4.7: When that teacher is seated upon the seat most highly honored, then you shall tell whatever that best of the twice-born asks of you.
t.1.4.8: So be it. When that great-souled teacher has taken his seat, then, questioned by him, I shall tell holy tales resting on many themes.
t.1.4.9: Then that bull among brahmins, having performed all his duties in due order and having satisfied the gods with words of praise and the ancestors with offerings of water, came there.
t.1.4.10: There the perfected brahmarṣis, firm in their vows, were seated, having taken their place at the sacrificial enclosure, with the son of the sūta at their head.
t.1.4.11: Then, when the officiating priests and the members of the assembly had taken their seats, Śaunaka, the master of the house, being himself seated, then spoke these words.
